items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: He asked me to do a couple of recordings with him, and we went up to Decca and recorded

ctx.x: And as I say, never a bad night. And it was also -- we used to play medleys, and there were some beautiful things; Cutty Cutshall on trombone would play something, everybody took turns with the medleys, and I had an association with Edmund

Hall, who was wonderful. He asked me to do a couple of recordings with him, and we went up to Decca and recorded -- "Big 'n' a" with him, we Ralph Sutton was on piano, and he took Walter Page up, and we made one or two recordings or albums -- I forget which; there was a transition then from 78's into LP's, and I never received those recordings. Somebody played them for me at a hall once, and I asked them who was playing brushes, who the drummer was -- I didn't even recognize my own playing. I felt very…

However -- at this time, I was in to the Hit Parade, which I did on weekends, and my reputation was growing there. I was fortunate to be able to read and cut a few parts, and I was hired by contractors, I had a reputation of working on the Hit Parade, which was a great show in those days -- I was hired, I ws what you'd call on the 'outside'. A freelance artist. But I was still working nights until four o'clock in the morning, which was killing at times.
